According to the document "A Sugar-Derived Room-Temperature Sodium Sulfur Battery with Long Term Cycling Stability" (nanolett-6b05172), page 6:

"At 1C, a cathode tested at higher rates revealed similar behavior but after initial decay exhibited extremely stable capacity with 306 mAh/gS delivered at cycle 1500."

The reversible capacity at 1C in the rate test was 370 mAh/gS (page 5, Figure 2C). 

To find the share of the capacity at cycle 1500 of the reversible capacity at 1C in the rate test, we calculate:

(306 mAh/gS / 370 mAh/gS) * 100 = 82.7%

So, the capacity per gram of sulfur delivered at cycle 1500 at 1C is 306 mAh/gS, which is 82.7% of the reversible capacity at 1C in the rate test.
